pairs.subject: data-access
pairs.evidence: crates/table-core/src/lib.rs:1 table-core is the pure domain crate the data layer depends on: its Cargo.toml declares only serde/serde_json/serde_jcs/thiserror/sha2/ulid/ts-rs, and a case-insensitive search of the crate for rusqlite, sqlx, transaction, repository and connection found nothing, so no store seam exists here and the repository doctrine has nothing to govern beyond the closed query vocabulary it hands down.

techniques.evidence: crates/table-core/src/book.rs:14 Analytical queries are a closed serde enum vocabulary (BookView/BookField/BookOp/BookGroup/BookMetric) with deny_unknown_fields; an unknown field token fails to deserialize and is never passed through. The crate-level doc at book.rs:1 states no SQL string is in the public schema. The token-to-column mapping lives in table-ledger and is outside this context.

crates/table-core/src/lib.rs:38 The domain imports nothing above it. Time is injected through a trait, and IO and storage are supplied by callers, so the arrow points one way: the data layer depends on these types and never the other way round.

crates/table-core/src/deal.rs:139 No row decode happens here. The crate only supplies one authoritative state list (RELEASED) that the ledger's SQL filter reuses, which is a vocabulary authority rather than a mapper.
crates/table-core/src/lib.rs:1 There are no writes and no transaction boundary; all IO belongs to callers.
crates/table-core/src/lib.rs:1 There is no fetch surface, so there are no round trips.
crates/table-core/src/lib.rs:1 There is no repository to test against an engine.
crates/table-core/src/lib.rs:37 Nothing here writes to a stream; the crate only defines the timestamp type, which callers supply.
crates/table-core/src/lib.rs:1 No storage drivers are present.
crates/table-core/src/lib.rs:1 No store interface has multiple implementations.
crates/table-core/src/book.rs:5 The crate names the views as a closed vocabulary, but projection queries are computed in the ledger, not here.
